analysis.investment_thesis: Chalet is a quality hospitality operator riding India's post-COVID travel recovery, but at 28x P/E and 16.8x EV/EBITDA the market is already pricing in a seamlessly perfect upcycle with zero allowance for mean reversion. The second-level question is: net profit already fell 49% from FY2024 to FY2025 (INR 278 Cr to INR 142 Cr) while consensus celebrates — that disconnect is the red flag, not the headline.
key_strengths: Strong EBITDA growth: 14% CAGR over 9 years with operating CF of INR 950 Cr in FY2025 demonstrating real cash generation ability
Operating margin of 35.5% is high for the sector, reflecting premium positioning in business hotels
Equity base more than doubled to INR 3,415 Cr in FY2025 (likely QIP), meaningfully reducing balance sheet risk and bringing D/E to 0.73x
key_risks: Free cash flow turned negative in FY2025 (-INR 14 Cr) due to INR 969 Cr capex — the expansion bet must deliver or destroy value
Net profit is structurally volatile and already declining YoY despite a supposed boom cycle — very low margin of safety at current price
Hotels are among the most COVID/recession-vulnerable assets: FY2021 saw revenue collapse 71% and near-zero EBITDA — the cycle will turn
red_flags: Net profit DOWN 49% YoY (INR 278 Cr → INR 142 Cr) even while revenue grows — operating leverage is not flowing through
ROE of only 5.77% at current prices is deeply inadequate for the cyclical risk being taken
FCF yield is effectively zero/negative while capex is accelerating — owners are not seeing cash returns at the current price
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Chalet sits at the intersection of a popular consensus trade (India hospitality boom) and a dangerous valuation setup. At 28x P/E on shrinking net profits and 16.8x EV/EBITDA on peak-ish EBITDA, the price reflects flawless execution of a large capex program (INR 969 Cr in FY2025 alone) against a favorable macro backdrop — neither of which is guaranteed. The second-level thinker asks: if FY2025 already shows profit compression despite a good travel environment, what does a mild slowdown do to this stock?

The balance sheet is cleaner after the equity raise, but cash absorption from investing activities (INR -1,355 Cr in FY2025) vastly exceeded operating inflows. The business has never demonstrated the ability to sustain earnings through a full cycle — losses in 2016, 2018, 2019, 2021, and 2022 reveal the true earnings power of this asset. Paying 28x P/E for a cyclical with this track record leaves essentially no margin of safety.
